newsitem.title: INDIA: India's "fodder" scandal stretches back a decade.
newsitem.headline: India's "fodder" scandal stretches back a decade.

text.p: A $280 million scandal over the use of state animal welfare funds which rocked Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's party on Monday stretches back more than a decade but only came to light in January last year.

Authorities in the eastern state of Bihar ordered raids on the offices of the Animal Husbandry Department in January lst year after officers discovered what appeared to be excessive withdrawals from the state treasury over a period extending into the mid-1980s.
The state government then set up a one-man judicial commission on March 10 last year to conduct a probe into the "animal fodder" case.
One day later, the state high court ordered the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal police force, to investigate the matter.
The CBI questioned Laloo Prasad Yadav, Bihar chief minister and head of Gujral's Janata Dal party, this January 6.
Earlier the agency had interrogated junior Rural Areas and Employment Minister Chandradeo Prasad Varma as well as Jagannath Mishra, former Bihar chief minister and a Congress party leader.
The CBI said on Monday it had decided to prosecute Yadav -- known in India as Laloo -- as well as Varma, Mishra and 53 others. Yadav, Varma and Mishra have said they are innocent.
The CBI has already filed 12 indictments against 46 people in the case. But it must receive authorisation from Bihar governor A.R. Kidwai to indict Yadav as he is a sitting chief minister.
If the governor sanctions the move, the CBI will charge Yadav with violating the Prevention of Corruption Act, which carries a maximum penalty of seven years in jail, CBI officials said.
CBI officials said the agency would also need the Bihar governor's authorisation to indict Varma as he was a state official when the alleged misuse of funds occurred.
